module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1025

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1025](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1025)
- [Er71] Erdős, P., *Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis*.
  Combinatorial Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97-109.
- [ErHa58] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A., *On the structure of set mappings*. Acta Math. Acad. Sci.
  Hungar. (1958), 111-133.
- [Sp72] Spencer, Joel, *Turán's theorem for $k$-graphs*. Discrete Math. (1972), 183--186.
- [CFS16] Conlon, David and Fox, Jacob and Sudakov, Benny, *Short proofs of some extremal results
  II*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B (2016), 173--196.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Asymptotics

namespace Erdos1025

/-- `X` is independent for a set mapping `f` on pairs if `f s(x, y) ∉ X` whenever `x ≠ y` are in
`X`. -/
def IsIndependent {n : ℕ} (f : Sym2 (Fin n) → Fin n) (X : Finset (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∀ x ∈ X, ∀ y ∈ X, x ≠ y → f s(x, y) ∉ X

/-- `g n` is the largest `k` such that every set mapping `f` on the pairs of an `n`-element set
with `f(x, y) ∉ {x, y}` admits an independent set of size at least `k`. -/
noncomputable def g (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup {k : ℕ | k ≤ n ∧ ∀ f : Sym2 (Fin n) → Fin n,
    (∀ x y, x ≠ y → f s(x, y) ≠ x ∧ f s(x, y) ≠ y) →
      ∃ X : Finset (Fin n), IsIndependent f X ∧ k ≤ X.card}

/--
Let $f$ be a function from all pairs of elements in $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ to $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ such
that $f(x,y)\neq x$ and $\neq y$ for all $x,y$. We call $X\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ independent
if whenever $x,y\in X$ we have $f(x,y)\not\in X$.

Let $g(n)$ be such that, in every function $f$, there is an independent set of size at least
$g(n)$. Estimate $g(n)$.

A question of Erdős and Hajnal [ErHa58], who could prove $n^{1/3} \ll g(n) \ll (n\log n)^{1/2}$.
Spencer [Sp72] proved $g(n)\gg n^{1/2}$. Conlon, Fox, and Sudakov [CFS16] proved
$g(n)\ll n^{1/2}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos1025.lean#L829"]
theorem erdos_1025 : (fun n : ℕ => (g n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] fun n : ℕ => √n := by
  sorry

end Erdos1025

findings.description: The module bibliography gives the page range of [ErHa58], “On the structure of set mappings,” as 111–133 (line 28). The paper ends on page 131. This is only a reference error; the mathematical declarations are unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: The original paper at https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1958-12.pdf ends with its references on page 131. The Rényi bibliography and reference [20] of Conlon–Fox–Sudakov also give Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. 9 (1958), 111–131.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the [ErHa58] page range from `111-133` to `111-131`.

reformulations.difference: The sources use maps on genuine two-element subsets. Lean uses `Sym2 (Fin n)`, which additionally contains diagonal pairs, but excludes those pairs from both admissibility and independence conditions.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Restricting a Lean map to non-diagonal pairs preserves admissibility and every independent set. Conversely, a map on distinct pairs extends to all of `Sym2` by assigning the repeated vertex to each diagonal pair; these new values are never tested. I proved the equivalence of the universally guaranteed-size predicates in `scratch.lean`, and proved equality between this file's `g` and the cited proof's distinct-pair extremal function in `proof_bridge.lean`.

sources_consulted: Erdős, Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis (1971), problem 19, p. 106: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1971-25.pdf
Erdős–Hajnal, On the structure of set-mappings (1958), introductory definitions, Problem 4, and Theorem 12: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1958-12.pdf
Conlon–Fox–Sudakov, Short proofs of some extremal results II, §2, LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1507.00547v2
https://api.elsevier.com/content/article/PII:0012365X72900842?httpAccept=text%2Fxml — Spencer publisher metadata; full text was unavailable.
https://cims.nyu.edu/~spencer/ and https://cims.nyu.edu/~spencer/papers/papers.html — searched the author's publication listings.
Local Mathlib sources: Mathlib/Data/Sym/Sym2.lean, Mathlib/Order/Lattice/Nat.lean, and Mathlib/Analysis/Asymptotics/Defs.lean.
review.notes: All three declarations were checked; no mathematical misformalization was found. The supremum defining g is nonempty, bounded, and attained. Lean checks establish g(0),…,g(4) = 0,1,2,2,2, admissible maps for every n ≥ 3, and the usual positive-constant two-sided interpretation of Θ. The cited proof was kernel-checked with its namespace renamed and the required initial portion of its dependency compiled. A proved bridge yields the exact reviewed theorem with axioms only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], without using the repository's sorry theorem. Spencer's full text could not be retrieved, but its applicable bound is explicitly stated and explained in CFS16 §2. Scratch files and proof-audit results are under /workspace/review/.
